summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for severe constipation and associated nausea, with a background of type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and autonomic neuropathy. She also reported chronic fatigue, chills, and orthostatic symptoms. Constipation was treated successfully with an aggressive bowel regimen, leading to symptom resolution. Hyponatremia and acute kidney injury were attributed to dehydration and improved with IV fluids; Lasix was discontinued. Orthostatic hypotension was managed with hydration and compression stockings. Evaluation for fatigue showed no cardiac, endocrine, or infectious causes; obstructive sleep apnea and psychiatric factors were considered contributors. She was discharged home with a new daily laxative regimen, reduced diltiazem, and follow-up plans for sleep study, CPAP refit, and outpatient management of diabetes and kidney disease.
